In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Commentary on Surat Nuh, peace be upon him

It is Meccan.

He is Nuh son of Lamak son of Mutawshalakh son of Akhnukh.

It is related from Ibn 'Abbas that he was sent as a prophet at the age of forty.

It is related from 'Awf ibn Abi Shaddad that he was sent as a prophet at the age of three hundred and fifty.

It is said: he was named Nuh because he used to lament (yanuh) over himself.

And Allah knows best.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Indeed, We sent Nuh to his people, [saying]: Warn your people before there comes to them a painful punishment﴾. Its meaning: "that you warn your people," except that the preposition (ba') has been omitted.

In the recitation of Ibn Mas'ud it is ﴿warn your people﴾ without "an" (that), and its meaning is: "We said to him: warn your people."

His saying ﴿before there comes to them a painful punishment﴾: it is said that it is drowning in this world. And it is said that it is the Fire in the Hereafter.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 71, verse 2:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿He said, "O my people, indeed I am to you a clear warner."﴾ That is: clearly warning.

And His saying ﴿That worship Allah, fear Him, and obey me﴾. This is the very purpose for which Allah sent the messengers, for Allah the Exalted did not send any messenger except that they might worship Him, fear Him, and obey His messenger.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 71, verse 4:

And His saying: ﴿He will forgive you of your sins﴾ means: of your sins for which He threatened you with punishment.

And they had other sins, from which Allah pardoned them.

Al-Farra' said: "Min" (from) here is not for partition (tab'id), but for specification (takhsis), in the sense of specifying sins for forgiveness.

And His saying: ﴿and defer you until a named term﴾ means: until death.

If it is said: this verse indicates that a person may have two terms, and that punishment may befall before the term appointed for death.

The answer has two aspects. The first: it may be said that the term is of two kinds: one, until a year or two years if they disobey Allah; and the other, until ten or twenty years if they obey Allah. On this basis, His saying the Exalted: ﴿When the term of Allah comes, it is not deferred﴾ means: in both states, obedience and disobedience.

The second aspect: the term is one in every case.

And His saying ﴿and defer you until a named term﴾ means: He will cause you to die a death other than the death of annihilation and punishment, namely the death that occurs without drowning, killing, or burning.

It was also said: "defer you until a named term" means: with you, which is the term you know, and that is death by means other than these.

This view is closer to the doctrine of the People of the Sunnah. On this basis, His saying: ﴿When the term of Allah comes, it is not deferred﴾ is the named term appointed for every person.

And His saying ﴿if you only knew﴾ [means]: if you were to know.

Almighty Allah's words: ﴿He said, "My Lord, I have called my people night and day"﴾. Al-Farra' said: that is, from every direction and at every time in which calling them was possible, whether by night or by day.
And His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿But my calling them has only increased them in flight﴾. That is: in flight from faith.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 71, verse 7:

And His saying: ﴿And indeed, every time I call them, that You may forgive them﴾ means: that they may believe, so that You may forgive them. He used forgiveness as a metaphor (kināya) for faith, because faith is the cause of forgiveness.

And His saying: ﴿They put their fingers in their ears﴾ means: they did that so that they would not hear.

And His saying: ﴿And they covered themselves with their garments﴾ means: they wrapped themselves in their clothes so that they would not see Nuh and would not hear his speech. Al-Nahhas (Abu Ja'far al-Nahhas) mentioned another opinion and said: the meaning of His saying ﴿and they covered themselves with their garments﴾ is: they displayed enmity.

It is said: "So-and-so put on the garments of enmity," meaning he openly displayed enmity.

And His saying: ﴿And persisted﴾. Abu 'Ubayd said: [i.e.] they remained upon it.

Persistence (al-israr) is to do an action and then not feel remorse for it.

In some rare reports it is narrated: "There is no minor sin with persistence, and no major sin with seeking forgiveness."

And His saying: ﴿And they were arrogant with great arrogance﴾ means: they acted with great pride.

We have already explained that polytheism and the refusal to affirm monotheism (tawhid) is arrogance.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 71, verses 8–10:

The Exalted said: ﴿Then indeed I called them openly. Then indeed I proclaimed to them and I spoke to them in private, a secret speech.﴾ If it is said: Does this not fall under the Exalted's words: (My Lord, indeed I have called my people night and day)? We say: The speech may be such that he said this for emphasis, and "proclamation" (i'lan) and "openly" (jahr) have one meaning, and it is speech such that a group can hear it. And "secret speech" (israr) is that he says it to a person alone, in seclusion.

The second answer: The meaning of his words ﴿I have called my people night and day﴾ is a call to monotheism (tawhid). As for his words ﴿Then indeed I called them openly. Then indeed I proclaimed to them and I spoke to them in private, a secret speech﴾, it is his calling them to seeking forgiveness (istighfar) for what follows it, which is the Exalted's words: {So I said: Seek forgiveness from your Lord; indeed He is ever Forgiving} (Qur'an 71:10).

The Exalted said: ﴿Then indeed I called them openly. Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 71, verse 11:

And His saying: ﴿He will send the sky upon you in abundant rain﴾ means: "so that He may send" (the particle lam of purpose is implied, i.e., *li-yursila*).

"Midrāran" means: continuously, in succession.

"Al-samā'" (the sky) here means: the rain.

It was also said that it refers to the rain in its proper season.

In some reports: when Allah intends good for a people, He sends them rain at the time of sowing, and withholds it from them at the time of harvest; and when He intends evil for a people, He sends them rain at the time of harvest and withholds it at the time of sowing.

Al-Sha'bi narrated that ʿUmar (may Allah be pleased with him) once went out to seek rain (istisqa') and did not do more than seek forgiveness (istighfar), then he came down.

It was said to him: "O Commander of the Faithful, you did not seek rain!" He said: "I have indeed sought rain through the constellations (majadih) of the sky by which rain is drawn down," and he recited His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Ask forgiveness of your Lord; indeed He is ever Forgiving﴾.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 71, verse 12:

And His saying: ﴿And He will increase you in wealth and sons﴾. Qatadah said: He knew that the people were men of this world, so He moved them through it so that they would believe.

It is related from some of them: that Allah the Exalted made the wombs of their women barren for forty years, and withheld the rain from them for forty years. This is the meaning of Nuh's saying: ﴿He will send the sky upon you in abundant rain, and increase you in wealth and sons﴾.

And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And He will make for you gardens and make for you rivers﴾, meaning: orchards, and rivers flowing among them.

The Words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿What is the matter with you that you do not expect dignity from Allah?﴾ That is: you do not fear the greatness and power of Allah.

Qatrub said: "What is the matter with you that you do not care about the greatness of Allah the Exalted?"

It was also said: "waqaran" means obedience, and the meaning is: "What is the matter with you that you do not hope for obedience to Allah," that is, you do not put it into practice.

The first opinion is the well-known one, mentioned by al-Farra' (al-Farra'), al-Zajjaj (al-Zajjaj) and others. The word rajaa' (hope) is sometimes used in the sense of khawf (fear), because hope is never without a accompanying fear of missing out.

A poet said:

(When the bees sting him, he does not hope for their sting... and he opposes them in a house of the nawb (a kind of wasp?) ('awamil))

Another said:

(When the people of honour treat me honourably, I do not hope for humiliation from the base.)

That is: I do not fear.

And His saying: ﴿And He has created you in stages﴾. Abu 'Ubayda said: al-tawr (stage, state) means al-hal (condition).

Ibn al-Anbari also mentioned it.

The poet said:

(A man is created, stage after stage [atwar])

The meaning of "states" here is that He created him as a drop of fluid, then a clinging clot, then a lump of flesh, then bone, and clothed the bone with flesh, until He perfected his creation.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 71, verse 15:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Have you not considered how Allah created seven heavens in layers?﴾ We have already explained it.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 71, verse 16:

And His saying: ﴿And made the moon therein a light﴾. If someone says: The moon was only created in the lowest heaven, so how does He say: ﴿therein a light﴾?

The answer comes in several respects. The first: it is permissible in the Arabic language to say "therein a light" even though it is in one of them (the heavens), as a man says: "So-and-so hid himself in the houses of so-and-so," although he hid himself in only one of them.

And the speaker says: "He alighted among the Banu Tamim," although he alighted with only some of them.

.

The second respect: what 'Abdullah ibn 'Amr ibn al-'As said, that the face of the moon is toward the seven heavens and its back toward the earth, and he said the same of the sun. On this view, His saying ﴿therein a light﴾ means: its light is in them.

The third respect: the heavens, in meaning, are like one thing, so He said ﴿therein a light﴾ for this reason, even though it is in one heaven.

The fourth respect: the meaning of His saying ﴿therein a light﴾ is: ﴿with them a light﴾.

Imru' al-Qays said:

(And will they be pleased with one whose last covenant was thirty months, in three states?)

That is: with three states.

And His saying ﴿and made the sun a lamp﴾ means: therein, and the meaning is as we have explained.

It is also related from 'Abdullah ibn 'Amr that he said: "Allah has created nothing more intense in heat than the sun, and were it not that the sky stands between the earth and its light, it would burn everything on the earth."

And it is narrated that he was asked why time grows cold in winter and why heat occurs in summer. He said: "In summer the sun is in the lowest heaven, and in winter it is in the seventh heaven."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 71, verse 17:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And God has caused you to grow from the earth as a growth﴾. It is permissible in the language (lughah) for it to be ʾinbatan and nabatan.

It was also said: "He caused you to grow (anbatakum), so you grew (fanabtum) a growth (nabatan)."

And His saying: ﴿Then He will return you into it﴾, i.e., by death.

And His saying: ﴿and will bring you forth, a (true) bringing forth﴾, at the resurrection.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 71, verse 19:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And Allah has made the earth for you a spread-out carpet﴾. That is, He spread it out, spreading it wide.

And His saying: ﴿That you may traverse therein broad roads⁠﴾. That is: wide paths.

The word sabil (سبيل, "path, way") may be used both as masculine and feminine.

The poet says:

(Men wish that I would die, and if I die, / then that is a path in which I am not unique.)

That is: "not a single one" (بواحد, bi-wahid), i.e., not alone.

And His saying: ﴿Noah said, "My Lord, they have disobeyed me and followed one whose wealth and children increase him only in loss."﴾ That is, the weak followed the nobles, the grandees and the leaders among the disbelievers, whose wealth and children increased them only in loss.
And their saying: ﴿And they schemed a great scheme﴾ means: a grand one. In the language, kibār is stronger than kabīr.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 71, verse 23:

And His saying: ﴿And they said, "Do not leave your gods"﴾, meaning: do not leave your gods. ﴿Nor leave Wadd or Suwa' or Yaghuth and Ya'uq and Nasr﴾, meaning: nor leave Wadd. These names are the names of their idols which they used to worship.

In the exegesis (tafsir) it is related that Wadd belonged to the tribe of Kalb, Suwa' belonged to Hudhayl, Yaghuth belonged to the Banu Ghutayf ibn Darim, Ya'uq belonged to Hamdan, and Nasr belonged to Himyar. It has also been said contrary to this.

The remaining idols of theirs had been from the time of Noah, and they had been drowned, so Iblis (Satan) brought them out for them until they worshipped them.

It is related from Abu 'Uthman al-Nahdi, who said: "Yaghuth was of lead; I saw it. When they travelled they would carry it on a bare-backed camel and would not provoke the camel, and they would place it in front of them. When it knelt down at a place, they would alight there and say: 'Your Lord is content with the stopping place.'"

It is related from Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi, who said: "These names are the names of righteous people before Noah. When they died, Satan adorned for their descendants the idea that they should take images in their likeness, so that looking at them would urge them to worship. Then they worshipped them after that, when time had lengthened for them."

The Exalted's saying: ﴿And they have led many astray﴾, meaning: many people went astray because of them.

And His saying: ﴿And do not increase the wrongdoers except in error﴾. He invoked this supplication against them as a punishment for them, and it is like Moses's supplication against the people of Pharaoh: ﴿Our Lord, obliterate their wealth and harden their hearts﴾.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 71, verse 25:

The words of the Exalted: ﴿Because of their sins they were drowned﴾, meaning: because of their sins. ﴿And then they were made to enter the Fire﴾, meaning: they were drowned in this world, and they were made to enter the Fire in the Hereafter.

It is also said: it refers to the grave.

It is narrated from al-Hasan, who said: "The sea is a layer of Jahannam."

It is also said: "The sea is fire upon fire."

And His words: ﴿They found for themselves no helpers besides Allah﴾, meaning: no one who could protect them from the punishment of Allah.

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And Noah said, "My Lord, do not leave upon the earth from among the disbelievers any dwellers."﴾ That is, anyone.

It was also said: "dayyaran" means one who dwells in a house (dar), derived from the word "dar" (house).

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Qur'an) on surah 71, verse 27:

And His saying: ﴿Indeed, if You leave them, they will mislead Your servants and will not beget except wicked disbelievers.﴾ This is in accordance with what Allah the Exalted informed about them: ﴿that none of your people will believe except those who have already believed﴾. And it is related from Mujahid that a man among them would come to Nuh and strike him until he lost consciousness; when he regained consciousness he would say: "O Allah, forgive my people, for they do not know."

Then, when Allah the Exalted informed him that none of them would believe, he invoked [destruction] upon them.

In the narrative: a man among them would carry his son on his shoulder to him and say: "Beware of this old man, the madman. If he refuses, let him warn you of himself as I warned you." They did this until seven generations had passed. It is reported that the last of them to come to him said the same to his son, and the boy said: "Put me down." So he put him down, and the boy began to throw stones at him until he wounded his head. He then became angry and invoked [destruction] upon them.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 71, verse 28:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿My Lord, forgive me and my parents﴾. Sa'id ibn Jubayr recited "li-wālidī" (to my father), and in some readings it is "li-wālidayya" (to my two parents).

And His saying: ﴿and whoever enters my house as a believer﴾, meaning: my ship.

It was also said: my hermitage (ṣawma'a).

It was also said: the house in which I dwell.

And His saying: ﴿and the believing men and believing women﴾, meaning: all believing men and women until the Day of Resurrection.

And His saying: ﴿and do not increase the wrongdoers except in ruin﴾, meaning: destruction.
